note: Not a missing URL and not a host problem: DOE renamed this laboratory, and the graph still carries the old name. DOE's own list of the national laboratories (https://www.energy.gov/national-laboratories, 10,425 readable chars) labels 16 of the 17 curated labs and not this one, because it prints the unit twice as a content label under 'National Laboratory of the Rockies' and explains in its own words: 'The National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR), formerly known as the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL), is a U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) national laboratory'. The laboratory's new site reads too (https://www.nlr.gov/, 1,201 readable chars): find_label_region_rule('National Laboratory of the Rockies') returns a hit in navigation, find_label_region_rule('National Renewable Energy Laboratory') returns None, and its footer reads 'The National Laboratory of the Rockies is a national laboratory of the U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation, operated under Contract No. DE-AC36-08GO28308.' So no URL fixes this: the page's own wording, for a curator, is 'National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR)', with the former name recoverable from DOE's own sentence. The queued candidate www.nrel.gov cannot answer either way — it serves no robots.txt and this project refuses such a host, which is what evidence.json already records for this node (fetch_failed, 2026-09-16), so the stale name has been hidden behind a host refusal. The prior agent on this shard probed the same DOE page and reported only that this lab was 'the one the DOE page does not label'; the reason it does not is on the page.
